name: What the Name-Wife Took
summary: Iffo Nauve, watchman of the South Stilts, paid the Name-Wife for his daughter's cure with his dead father's name, thinking it could cost a dead man nothing. Now nobody in Nauvissa remembers Oro Nauve, Iffo is losing his face, and the grey has started coming in over the scarp at night.
notes: Sedgemire world life, phase 2 (docs/WORLD_LIFE.md). The Name-Wife's Hollow (core:poi/name_wifes_hollow, a cave delve with core:interior/name_wifes_hollow and the Name-Wife as its boss). Crookstilts' price-slate points here. The choice is made with Iffo at the South Stilts.

stages.journal: Iffo Nauve went to the Name-Wife at Crookstilts at the dark of the moon and paid for his daughter's flats-cough with a name: his father's, Oro Nauve, twenty years drowned. The cure took. Now Oro's lantern goes unlit on the Long Night, his knot has come off the Tide Hearth, and Iffo cannot see his face. The Name-Wife keeps the names she takes knotted into cords in her hollow under the South Scarp, west of the Stilts where the scarp curls round a cove. Go in and bring back whatever she tied Oro Nauve into.

objectives.text: Find the Name-Wife's hollow under the South Scarp
Face the Name-Wife at the back of her hollow
Take the hank of names she carried

stages.journal: The Name-Wife carried the names she had not hung yet on her belt, in a hank as thick as an arm: a hundred cords and more, every one in a family's weave. Near the outside, still green, is a boatwright's splice. Iffo Nauve is on the South Stilts, watching the grey.

objectives.text: Settle with Iffo Nauve what is to be untied

options.text: Untie his father's cord, only his.
Untie every cord at the Tide Hearth and let every name go home, cures or no cures.

stages.journal: That night the grey sat on the lip of the South Scarp where it had sat for twenty years, and did not come down, and Iffo Nauve tied no knot on the rail.

name: The Sounding
summary: From the top of Heron Watch, Tuo Lissa has watched a tower go up on the North Shore and a bell go up into it. His sister Ama went to the Flood-Callers after her husband drowned, and the boats that pole north past the watch now go to the tower. She means to ring the bell from underneath.
notes: Sedgemire world life, phase 2 (docs/WORLD_LIFE.md). The Sounding (core:poi/the_sounding, a tower on a drowned platform with core:interior/the_sounding_undercroft and Ama Lissa as its boss). Follows on from The Lanterns Taken Up in the story, but does not need it. The choice is made with Tuo at Heron Watch.

stages.journal: Tuo Lissa has knotted a tower into the watch's rope: it has gone up on the North Shore, east of Mor'oul, on an old platform of the Builders' black stone, and this month a bell went up into it. The Flood-Callers' boats pole north past Heron Watch to it every night. His sister Ama is with them. She knotted the watch's rope with him as a girl; her husband went into the water off the Gullhithe flats and his lantern went out before it had burned a verse. Tuo says she means to ring the bell from underneath, where the drowned are. Go to the Sounding, and down.

objectives.text: Go to the Sounding on the North Shore
Stop the Sounder at the well under the platform
Take the bell-rope from the Sounder's hands

stages.journal: The bell-rope Ama Lissa held at the well is knotted its whole length in the Heron Watch knots. Read as Tuo reads his: a loop, a boat went north; nothing came back; nothing came back. Tuo Lissa is at Heron Watch, at the bottom of the ladder.

objectives.text: Give Tuo Lissa his sister's rope, and say what happened

options.text: Tell him the truth, and let him knot her rope into the watch's.
Tell him she went into the well, and send the rope out after her with a lantern.
Tell him she was gone before you got there, and keep the rope.

stages.journal: At the spring tide the bell in the Sounding hung still, and the water came up to the platform's lip and no further, the way it always had.
